key_insight: An AI-based facial grading system matched expert consensus well for larger shape-related and some lesion-based facial features, even when images were captured with less controlled smartphone settings.
clinical_relevance: This suggests AI-assisted facial assessment could help scale dermatology studies and hybrid/decentralized clinical trials by enabling objective grading outside specialized imaging studios.
method: Compared AI grading with expert panel consensus across standardized studio, clinic smartphone, and home smartphone image settings.
Evaluated repeatability on independently captured images and agreement across feature types.
Assessed performance for geometric, textural, pigmentation, and inflammatory facial endpoints.
evidence_signal: Experts showed good-to-excellent inter-rater reliability (median ICC 0.84-0.90), and the AI system showed very high test-retest repeatability (median ICC 0.97-0.98) with strongest agreement for macro-geometric features and moderate agreement for pigmented spot density.
watch_item: Performance dropped for fine-texture and color-dependent features under less controlled acquisition, so these endpoints may be less reliable in home smartphone workflows.
paper_title: Comparison of Facial Feature Grading by an AI-Based System Versus Human Expert Grading on Images Under Standardized Clinical and At-Home Settings
